name: othername-san-with-noncritical-unknown-constraint-invalid
description: An intermediate carries a non-critical nameConstraints extension that permits an otherName with an unknown OID, and the leaf has an otherName SAN with that exact OID. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 says restrictions apply only when the specified name form is present in the leaf - it IS present here - so the verifier must evaluate the SAN against the (unspecified-semantics) constraint, and the only safe default is to reject.
notes: The criticality of the nameConstraints extension itself is a red herring. RFC 5280 4.2 says non-critical extensions may be ignored by verifiers that do not recognize the extension. A verifier that recognizes nameConstraints (and is enforcing it) must still apply this rule whether or not the extension is marked critical; criticality only affects what an UNAWARE verifier may do.

OpenSSL rejects with `unsupported name constraint type` (X509_V_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRAINT_TYPE). GnuTLS rejects as `chain violates the signer's constraints`. Both fail-close, which is the right default for an unknown-semantics constraint form whose name form IS present in the leaf.
Go accepts this chain, but appears to do so vacuously: Go's crypto/x509 does not apply otherName name-constraint matching at all.
